items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: I had to play Buster Bailey's book.

ctx.x: What about Fletcher? You knew him, I guess, over the years from just traveling and --

Well, I knew him, knew of Fletcher, but I really met him when I joined the band in California. And Fletcher Henderson was one of the nicest men you ever met. He was a very passive type of a person and very quiet. I remember when I -- this is really where I got together on my clarinet, in Fletcher's band, because when I went in Fletcher's band I had to play Buster Bailey's book. And the first week I quit. It was so -- the clarinet things were in such crazy keys and were so fast, and when I'd get up and play, I'd…

He sat near the piano, and he'd laugh and call it again. And I would play and mess it up, and he would -- and so I told him at the end of the first week, I said, 'Look, I am putting in my two weeks' notice.'

He says, 'What's the matter?' I says, 'I can't -- I'm not a clarinet player. I can't play these things. I mean, it's too big of a job.' He says, 'Aw, keep -- you're doing all right. Go ahead and keep trying.' So I started taking the book home.
